findings.title: New abstract interface method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `order()` is added to the public `CryptoProvider` interface as an abstract method with no default. Any third-party or out-of-tree implementation will stop compiling, or throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when `detectProvider` sorts the providers. Make it a `default` method returning a neutral value.

findings.title: Providers with equal order are chosen nondeterministically and silently
findings.body: Default, Elytron and FIPS providers all return order 200. Previously, multiple providers on the classpath failed fast. Now the stable sort keeps ServiceLoader order, which depends on classpath ordering, and the others are ignored with only a debug log. A FIPS deployment that accidentally has the default provider present could silently run non-FIPS crypto. Detect ties at the top order and throw, or at least warn.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an arbitrary keystore provider
findings.body: It returns the provider of the default KeyStore type (e.g. SUN for PKCS12). Callers that expect a BouncyCastle provider for algorithms such as ECDSA or PSS lookups will get a provider that lacks them, causing NoSuchAlgorithmException. It would be safer to return null, as Elytron does, or to document the behaviour.

findings.title: Indefinite length or malformed sequence handling
findings.body: `readLength` returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, and `readSequence` then silently returns an empty list. `readInteger` would call `new byte[-1]` and throw NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException. Malformed signatures therefore produce unexpected runtime exceptions. Reject -1 explicitly.
